title: The Reciter (Tanna) of the School of Rabbi So-and-so, or “A Reciter Taught before Rabbi So-and-so”
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: Hyman has already explained in several places that every head of an academy had a reciter (tanna) or reciters (tannaim) (even at the end of the period of the Amoraim) who sat before him and were very expert in the baraitot by heart. When a baraita was needed (for the most part they studied orally), he was like a living book and would tell his teacher the wording of the baraita. But since their whole concern was only to have the wording of the baraita fluent in their mouths, they sometimes erred in a word; and this is why we find many times in the Talmud that the head of the academy said to him, “Do not teach it so,” or “Delete it.” Hyman applies to them the statement in Sotah 22a: “The Tannaim destroy the world, for they rule halakhah from their mishnah” — this does not refer to our masters, the sages of the Mishnah or the baraitot, but to these reciters.
So Rashi wrote on Chullin 15a, s.v. Atu; and see Bava Metzia 34a, Rashi s.v. LeTannai.

So it is cited in the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, part 1, chapter 6, where he says: “And the Tannaim too learned them among themselves, such as Achi, the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Chiyya, and Bar Ashyan, the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Ami.”

notes.text: Tanna in this notice is a professional oral reciter, including in the late Amoraic period, not automatically a sage of the Mishnah. Hyman’s living-book account and interpretation of Sotah’s criticism are attributed. The doubled for is removed, and Achi/Bar Ashyan examples remain distinct.

Sotah 22a and its Rashi directly criticize mistaken rulings made from memorized Mishnah without knowing its reasons or the status of disputes. Hyman’s account of professional oral reciters, including late Amoraic reciters, remains his interpretation. The exact Chullin 15a, Bava Metzia 34a and Epistle editions cited here were not newly inspected, and the reciter label does not automatically date a person to the Mishnaic period.
